hypothesis: The parent's best result came from giving the timing-driven placer broader net weighting (lilith) and a looser density-weight band; the untested complement is to make the GNN partition itself timing-aware by weighting positive (same-partition-desired) contrastive pairs by edge timing criticality, so timing-critical neighbors are pulled into the same embedding cluster and thus more likely onto the same tier (short, same-tier paths that rsz can repair with bottom-tier buffers).
expected_effect: TNS improves on all three circuits (critical nets kept intra-tier -> shorter paths, fewer moderate violations); WNS flat-to-slightly-better; overflow unchanged; runtime unchanged.
analysis: The hypothesis held: making the GNN partition timing-aware improved all three cases (total +0.590, robust +0.181, all valid). Gains concentrate in WNS/TNS: bp-ng45 dWNS +10.3%/dTNS +28.1%, bp_fe-ng45 dWNS +21.3%, ariane133-ng45 dTNS +30.6%, with overflow modest (~105–132). Mechanism is consistent—timing-critical neighbors co-clustered onto the same tier, yielding short same-tier paths repairable by bottom-tier buffers. Next step: sweep the criticality weighting exponent (and cap) to test whether stronger timing bias further improves WNS without inflating overflow, and verify on additional seeds.
